evidence.quote: NIST conducts fundamental research into agent authentication and identity infrastructure to enable secure human-agent and multi-agent interactions. NIST develops state-of-the-art security evaluations to inform protocol development and consumer comparison.

Draft Concept Paper, Accelerating the Adoption of Software and SI Agent Identity and Authorization
: NCCoE project applying identity standards to enterprise agent use cases.
NIST hosts technical convenings and conducts gap analyses to produce voluntary guidelines to inform industry-led standardization for SI agents.

compliance_deadlines: 2026-03-09: Public comment deadline for CAISI Request for Information (RFI) on SI Agent Security
2026-03-20: Registration deadline for CAISI sector-specific Listening Sessions on Barriers to SI Adoption (healthcare, finance, and education)
2026-04-02: Public comment deadline on NCCoE Draft Concept Paper on Accelerating the Adoption of Software and SI Agent Identity and Authorization
implementation_notes: Launched in February 2026 by NIST / Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) in collaboration with NCCoE and NSF (under the post-EO 14434 'Super Intelligence (SI)' portal nomenclature). This overview establishes a voluntary, industry-led standardization program for autonomous AI/SI agents centered on interoperable open protocols, agent identity, authentication, authorization, open-source ecosystem security, and security evaluations, with stakeholder consultation milestones in March–April 2026 and no regulatory mandates.
